newsitem.title: UK: UK's SIB to review rules after Morgan probe.
newsitem.headline: UK's SIB to review rules after Morgan probe.

text.p: The UK's Securities & Investments Board (SIB) said on Thursday it plans to review its collective investment scheme rules in the wake of the probe into three European investment funds at Morgan Grenfell Asset Management.
"We will be reviewing our collective investment scheme rules, in particular, the valuation of unquoted securities and the position of prelisted stocks," an SIB spokesman said.
The spokesman said it was premature to say whether the review would lead to a tightening of rules, as the Daily Telegraph reported in Thursday's edition.

Trading in three European funds run by MGAM was suspended on Monday and resumed earlier today amid an investigation by British investments watchdog IMRO and MGAM itself into suspected irregularities at the funds involving unquoted securities.

At present, unquoted securities can make up a maximum 10 percent of unit trust funds unless it can be shown that the companies plan to float within 12 months. The three MGAM funds exceeded that proportion.
